question: Several weeks after starting a new medication for rheumatoid arthritis, a 44-year-old woman comes to the physician because of painful ulcers in her mouth. Oral examination shows inflammation and swelling of the tongue and oropharynx and ulcers on the buccal mucosa bilaterally. Skin examination shows soft tissue swelling over her proximal interphalangeal joints and subcutaneous nodules over her elbows. Serum studies show an alanine aminotransferase level of 220 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase level of 214 U/L, and creatinine level of 1.7 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely primary mechanism of action of the drug she is taking?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "New medication for rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Methotrexate" -> "Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase" -> "Decreased folate synthesis" -> "Mouth ulcers" -> 90%
CHAIN: "New medication for rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Methotrexate" -> "Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase" -> "Increased liver enzymes" -> "Elevated ALT and AST" -> 85%
CHAIN: "New medication for rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Methotrexate" -> "Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase" -> "Renal impairment" -> "Elevated creatinine" -> 80%
CHAIN: "New medication for rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Methotrexate" -> "Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase" -> "Subcutaneous nodules" -> "Common in rheumatoid arthritis" -> 75%
CHAIN: "New medication for rheumatoid arthritis" -> "Methotrexate" -> "Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase" -> "Inflammation and swelling of tongue and oropharynx" -> 85%
analysis: The patient is experiencing side effects consistent with methotrexate use, a common medication for rheumatoid arthritis. Methotrexate can cause oral ulcers, hepatotoxicity (elevated liver enzymes), and renal impairment. Its primary mechanism of action is the inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase, which interferes with DNA synthesis and cell replication.
